name: Zion National Park
blurb: Virgin River canyon, bighorn, mule deer and the lions and condors above them.

tip.title: Remove the mountain lions
tip.text: Lions are the top predator of mule deer and bighorn sheep. Set Mountain lion to -100% and watch deer and sheep, then the plants they browse and the scavengers that rely on kills.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Zion National Park, Desert bighorn sheep, California condor). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives plant growth on the canyon floor, though summer heat and dryness limit it.
Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.
A shrubby oak of the woodland and higher slopes whose acorns and leaves feed squirrels, mice and deer.
A dryland conifer of the pinyon-juniper woodland. Its berry-like cones are eaten by rock squirrels and browsers.
A desert cactus of the lower slopes. Bighorn sheep break open cacti with their horns to reach the moist flesh.

nodes.name: Desert grasses
nodes.desc: Bunchgrasses of the open desert and woodland floor, the main food of bighorn sheep and a staple for rabbits and mice.
The most commonly seen large mammal in the park, browsing shrubs and trees. A main prey of mountain lions and a source of carrion.

nodes.name: Desert bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: Eats mainly grasses, with cacti, sedges and forbs when grass is short. Reintroduced to Zion after being largely gone from southwestern Utah.
A large ground squirrel of rocky slopes that eats seeds, nuts and fruit, and is prey for hawks and eagles.
A small seed-eating rodent that is food for foxes, snakes and hawks.
Feeds on grasses and other plants at night and is eaten by foxes, hawks and eagles.
A climbing omnivore that eats rodents, rabbits and fruit. Named as one of the smaller predators in Zion.
A soaring raptor that hunts ground squirrels, rabbits, mice and snakes from the air.
An ambush predator of mice, small rabbits and lizards across the rocky desert slopes.
A clever omnivore and the most recorded bird near Zion; it picks at carrion alongside vultures.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Finds carrion by smell and rides canyon thermals, cleaning up dead deer, rabbits and rodents.
A huge scavenger that feeds mainly on large dead mammals such as deer. A pair nested in Zion in 2014, the first successful Utah breeding.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: The top predator in Zion. It prefers large prey such as mule deer and bighorn sheep, and its kills feed scavengers.
A powerful raptor listed among the park's birds of prey. It takes rabbits and ground squirrels.

story: Zion National Park in Utah sits where the Colorado Plateau, the Great Basin and the Mojave Desert meet. Its four life zones hold 289 bird species, 75 mammals, including 19 bats, and 32 reptiles. Desert bighorn sheep, rated sensitive to extinction, live in its canyons.
matters: Three regions meeting in one place give Zion unusual plant and animal variety. Zion Canyon is 15 miles long and up to 2,640 feet deep.
